item.title: Northview Chiefs fall to Destin 35-21 on homecoming night
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Destin struck first, scoring a touchdown and field goal to grab an early 10-0 lead. Northview answered back, however, and took a 14-10 halftime advantage heading into the break.…
item.content:encoded:
The Northview Chiefs' homecoming celebration in Bratt ended in disappointment Thursday night as the Destin Sharks dominated in the second half to secure a 35-21 victory.

Destin struck first, scoring a touchdown and field goal to grab an early 10-0 lead. Northview answered back, however, and took a 14-10 halftime advantage heading into the break.

The Sharks outscored the Chiefs significantly after intermission to put the game out of reach. The loss drops Northview's record as the football season continues into October.

item.content:encoded: Escambia County Fire Rescue has determined that stray embers from an outside fire sparked a residential blaze on Muscogee Road in Cantonment Thursday afternoon. Firefighters responded to the scene around 2:40 p.m. and brought the fire under control. The incident underscores the importance of properly monitoring and containing outdoor fires, particularly in residential areas where embers can travel and ignite nearby structures.

The event will feature local vendors selling handmade goods including crafts, art, holiday decorations, local honey, handmade jewelry, and baked goods. A fish fry will run from 11 a.m. until sold out, giving visitors a chance to grab lunch while they shop.

The Extravaganza offers a chance to support local artisans and craftspeople in the North Escambia area ahead of the holiday season.

item.title: Foley, Alabama approves new door-to-door solicitation rules

The Foley City Council voted to approve the measure, which creates new requirements that commercial solicitors must follow when visiting residential areas. The ordinance aims to establish…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Foley has adopted a new ordinance establishing regulations for door-to-door solicitation, according to a city news release reported by WKRG News 5. The Foley City Council voted to approve the measure, which creates new requirements that commercial solicitors must follow when visiting residential areas.

The ordinance aims to establish clearer guidelines for solicitation activity in the city, though specific details about the new requirements were not immediately available. The move reflects growing efforts by municipalities across the region to balance residents' preferences for privacy and safety with legitimate commercial activity.

item.title: Pensacola health clinics preparing for Medicaid changes affecting immigrant eligibility
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The changes are expected to affect how local clinics serve their patient base, though details on the specific timeline and scope of the…
item.content:encoded:
Community health clinics in Pensacola are bracing for operational and financial impacts as shifts in Medicaid eligibility rules for certain immigrant populations take effect, according to reporting from WEAR-TV.

The changes are expected to affect how local clinics serve their patient base, though details on the specific timeline and scope of the eligibility modifications remain in development. Health care providers in the area are working to understand how the policy adjustments will influence their operations, staffing, and ability to serve uninsured or underinsured patients.

Clinics across Pensacola and the surrounding region have historically served immigrant communities, and leaders are assessing what additional resources or alternative care pathways may be needed to maintain continuity of service. The full impact of the eligibility changes could reshape how local health care systems approach preventive care, emergency services, and chronic disease management in communities most affected by the policy shift.

More details on the specific timing and implementation of the Medicaid changes are expected to be clarified in the coming weeks.

The case drew significant attention across North Florida and the broader Gulf Coast region, as it involved a deputy-involved shooting that resulted in a…
item.content:encoded:
A jury has found former Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office deputy Eddie Duran not guilty of manslaughter in the May 2024 shooting death of Air Force Airman Roger Fortson, according to WKRG News 5.

The case drew significant attention across North Florida and the broader Gulf Coast region, as it involved a deputy-involved shooting that resulted in a fatality. The jury's verdict concludes the manslaughter charge against Duran following the incident at Fortson's Fort Walton Beach home.

Details surrounding the circumstances of the shooting and the jury's reasoning behind the acquittal were not immediately available. The case had been closely watched by law enforcement observers and community members concerned with use-of-force policies.

item.title: Okaloosa County Completes Paving of Nearly 200 Miles of Dirt Roads
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Okaloosa County commissioners announced Thursday that they have paved nearly all county-maintained dirt roads—about 200 miles total—ahead of schedule, thanks to a voter-approved infrastructure surtax passed in 2018. The project, which began as a modest "50 in 5" initiative by then-Commissioner Nathan Boyles in 2020, exceeded its original goal of…
item.content:encoded:
Okaloosa County commissioners announced Thursday that they have paved nearly all county-maintained dirt roads—about 200 miles total—ahead of schedule, thanks to a voter-approved infrastructure surtax passed in 2018.

The project, which began as a modest "50 in 5" initiative by then-Commissioner Nathan Boyles in 2020, exceeded its original goal of stabilizing 50 miles in five years. Instead, the county completed 180 miles of work in just four years, leaving only a handful of roads remaining. The improvements use a limerock base with either chip-seal or hot-mix asphalt topping.

"These are the types of projects that the residents expect from their government," said County Board Chairman Trey Goodwin in a statement. Officials say the paved roads will reduce long-term maintenance and fuel costs that previously went toward repairing washed-out dirt roads after heavy rain. Boyles, now a state representative, praised the county's continued investment in infrastructure. "As a taxpayer, I am proud that our County continues to wisely invest taxpayer money in infrastructure that makes our lives better," he said.

The county maintains a dashboard tracking current and completed infrastructure projects at myokaloosa.com/bcc/infrastructureprojects.

item.title: Walton Area Chamber Announces Keynote Speakers for Oct. 26 Business Conference
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Walton Area Chamber of Commerce is gearing up for its annual "The Next BIG Thing" conference on October 26th at the Hilton Sandestin Beach Golf Resort and Spa, with a lineup of three keynote speakers and nine breakout sessions designed to draw entrepreneurs and business leaders from across the region. The all-day event, presented by Ascension…
item.content:encoded:
The Walton Area Chamber of Commerce is gearing up for its annual "The Next BIG Thing" conference on October 26th at the Hilton Sandestin Beach Golf Resort and Spa, with a lineup of three keynote speakers and nine breakout sessions designed to draw entrepreneurs and business leaders from across the region.

The all-day event, presented by Ascension Sacred Heart Emerald Coast and Eglin Federal Credit Union, typically draws more than 250 attendees. The morning kicks off with Captain Kerry Titheradge, an international television personality and founder of Yachting Concepts LLC, who will speak on personal development and breaking out of comfort zones. Brian Franklin, co-founder and CEO of Vows & Speeches, will deliver the lunch keynote on finding your calling despite setbacks. Laura Quick, founder of Good Grit Magazine, will close the day discussing how mental health and personal growth impact leadership and business performance.

Attendees can choose from breakout sessions organized into three tracks: Leadership Development, Entrepreneurship, and Women in Business. The full-day experience includes breakfast with networking opportunities, complimentary professional headshots, lunch, and a closing cocktail hour with heavy hors d'oeuvres. Throughout the day, raffle prizes totaling thousands of dollars will be available to participants. For more information, contact Ali Weil at 334-328-1568 or ali@weilhousecreative.com.

item.title: Florida Backs Away From Expanding School Vaccine Exemptions
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Florida health officials are backing away from a proposal that would have expanded the reasons parents can exempt children from required school vaccinations. The Department of Health initially proposed allowing exemptions based on sincerely held moral or ethical beliefs, in addition to religion. A new filing removes that language, leaving…
item.content:encoded:
Florida health officials are backing away from a proposal that would have expanded the reasons parents can exempt children from required school vaccinations.


The Department of Health initially proposed allowing exemptions based on sincerely held moral or ethical beliefs, in addition to religion.


A new filing removes that language, leaving religious beliefs as the non-medical basis for an exemption.


The issue has local implications — the latest state data show about 87-percent of Escambia County students covered by immunization reporting were fully vaccinated last school year.

Pensacola International currently has about four-thousand parking spaces — roughly 25-percent more than it did several years ago.

item.title: Florida Highway Safety Dept. Launches October Pedestrian Safety Campaign
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles is kicking off National Pedestrian Safety Awareness Month with a reminder to both drivers and walkers to stay alert on Florida roads. Executive Director Dave Kerner emphasized that safety is a shared responsibility, urging motorists to slow down and remain aware of pedestrians, while…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles is kicking off National Pedestrian Safety Awareness Month with a reminder to both drivers and walkers to stay alert on Florida roads. Executive Director Dave Kerner emphasized that safety is a shared responsibility, urging motorists to slow down and remain aware of pedestrians, while pedestrians should stay visible and attentive.

The Florida Highway Patrol will join local law enforcement partners throughout October to reinforce safe travel practices. Colonel Gary Howze noted that "when everyone stays aware, Florida's roads become safer for all." The campaign targets common hazards, including distracted walking and driving, nighttime visibility issues, and unsafe crossing behavior.

The state recommends pedestrians use sidewalks when available, cross only at designated intersections and crosswalks, wear bright or reflective clothing at night, and avoid distractions like headphones or phones while crossing. Drivers are advised to slow down in school zones and neighborhoods, yield completely at crosswalks, and use extra caution in low-visibility conditions such as rain or darkness.

According to FLHSMV, pedestrians should never assume a driver sees them and should make eye contact with approaching vehicles when possible. The agency also clarified that all sides of an intersection count as crosswalks—marked or unmarked—unless officially closed and posted as such.

item.title: PPD: Bullet Narrowly Misses Sleeping Resident, Chick-fil-A Crash Caused $50K in Damage
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola Police are investigating an early-morning incident in which a bullet fired inside a second-floor apartment traveled through the floor and narrowly missed a person sleeping in the apartment below. Public Information Officer Mike Wood discussed the investigation and several other local law enforcement…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola Police are investigating an early-morning incident in which a bullet fired inside a second-floor apartment traveled through the floor and narrowly missed a person sleeping in the apartment below.


Public Information Officer Mike Wood discussed the investigation and several other local law enforcement topics Thursday during an interview on NewsRadio 92.3's Pensacola's Morning News. Wood also provided new information about Wednesday's crash into the Chick-fil-A on Bayou Boulevard, clarified police findings involving an incident at Palafox Market and discussed emerging technology being used by law enforcement agencies to stop fleeing vehicles.


Bullet travels through apartment floor, narrowly misses resident

Wood said police responded early Thursday after a gunshot was fired inside a second-floor apartment on Royce Street.


The bullet traveled through the floor and entered a bedroom in the apartment below, narrowly missing a person who was in bed. No one was injured.

Officers traced the shot to the upstairs apartment and spoke with a woman inside. Wood said she initially gave an officer permission to look through the apartment, but then said she needed to use the bathroom.


The officer checked the bathroom first for possible weapons and instead found what Wood described as approximately a pound of marijuana in the toilet.

The woman later withdrew permission for officers to search the apartment, prompting investigators to obtain a search warrant.


As of Thursday morning, police had not located the gun and were still working to determine how the weapon was fired. Wood said investigators had not yet determined whether the shooting was accidental, intentional or involved some other circumstance.

He said charges are expected as the investigation continues.


PPD estimates $50,000 in damage from Chick-fil-A crash

Wood also provided additional details about Wednesday's crash into the Chick-fil-A on Bayou Boulevard.

According to police, two vehicles were traveling west on Bayou Boulevard when the vehicle in the right lane struck the curb. Wood said it then bounced into the vehicle traveling beside it before veering back to the right, leaving the roadway and crashing into the restaurant.

The driver suffered minor injuries. No one inside the Chick-fil-A was injured.

Wood estimated the crash caused approximately $50,000 in damage to the building.


Police clarify rules following Palafox Market incident

Wood also addressed questions surrounding a recent incident involving an individual at Palafox Market.


According to Wood, PPD and city legal staff reviewed the issue and determined that people generally retain the right to engage in otherwise lawful activity at an event held on public property when access to the event is not controlled.


Wood said that applies to Palafox Market because the event does not have a fenced perimeter or other controlled entrance.


Even when an event has a permit, Wood said an individual can generally remain in the public area and hold a sign, provided that person is not violating a law or ordinance.

Police will still respond when called, but Wood said once officers determine no law or ordinance is being violated, they will move along.


Wood distinguished that from an event where organizers establish a controlled perimeter and regulate admission. In those circumstances, organizers have greater control over who is permitted inside the event area.


The discussion followed a recent incident at Palafox Market that prompted questions about when someone can be trespassed from a permitted event on public property.


Vehicle-stopping 'Grappler' technology discussed

Wood also discussed a law enforcement tool known as the Grappler, which allows an officer pursuing a vehicle to deploy heavy-duty nylon webbing around one of the fleeing vehicle's rear wheels.


The device is mounted to the front of a police vehicle. Once an officer gets close enough, the webbing is deployed and wraps around the target vehicle's wheel and axle, preventing the wheel from continuing to turn and helping bring the vehicle to a stop.

Wood discussed the technology following its use in Kentucky during the apprehension of a suspect accused of fatally shooting a state trooper.


Wood said he was not aware of Pensacola Police currently using Grapplers and estimated the systems cost roughly $5,000 to $10,000 depending on the police vehicle.


He noted that while the technology can stop a fleeing vehicle without the type of collision associated with some other pursuit-ending tactics, it requires the pursuing officer to get extremely close to the suspect's vehicle.

During the interview, Wood was informed that the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office has Grappler-equipped vehicles.


Wood continues support for license plate reader technology

The conversation also returned to automated license plate readers, including Flock cameras.

Wood cited the Kentucky case as an example of license plate reader technology being used to help locate a wanted suspect.


Asked whether Pensacola Police had encountered any local cases during the past week where the absence of Flock cameras hindered an investigation, Wood said he was not aware of one.


He said agencies that continue to use the technology regularly report successful results and expressed hope that similar technology will eventually return locally in some form.

Wood serves as the Pensacola Police Department's public information officer and regularly provides information to local media on department investigations and public safety issues.

item.title: Escambia County Launches Annual Peanut Butter Challenge Food Drive
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: UF/IFAS Escambia Extension is kicking off its annual Peanut Butter Challenge today, seeking donations of unopened, unexpired peanut butter jars through November 20 to support local food pantries. The friendly statewide competition among Florida counties is coordinated by UF/IFAS Extension and Florida A&M University Cooperative Extension. Escambia…
item.content:encoded:
UF/IFAS Escambia Extension is kicking off its annual Peanut Butter Challenge today, seeking donations of unopened, unexpired peanut butter jars through November 20 to support local food pantries. The friendly statewide competition among Florida counties is coordinated by UF/IFAS Extension and Florida A&M University Cooperative Extension.

Escambia County residents can drop off donations at 12 locations throughout the county, including the Escambia County Administration building, Cordova Lanes, several churches, the Molino Library, and the Escambia Extension Office at 3740 Stefani Road. Last year, Escambia County led the entire state in total jars collected, bringing in 4,214 donations.

"Escambia County had incredible support from our community last year, and I hope to bring that same momentum to this year's challenge," said Nick Simmons, Escambia Extension Services Director. Peanut butter was selected as the challenge's focus item because of its nutritional value, long shelf life, and to highlight Florida's significant peanut production, which contributed over $168 million to the state's economy in 2025.

In addition to community donations, the Florida Peanut Producers Association and Florida Peanut Federation will also contribute to totals distributed to food pantries in their respective regions. For more information or to participate, contact Escambia Extension at 850-475-5230 or visit sfyl.ifas.ufl.edu/peanutbutter.

item.title: FDLE Warns of Cryptocurrency Scams Using AI, Warrant Claims
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Florida law enforcement is warning about new twists on cryptocurrency scams. FDLE says criminals are increasingly pitching fake investments claiming cryptocurrency will be used to buy equipment or infrastructure for artificial intelligence processing. Other scammers are demanding cryptocurrency payments for supposed arrest warrants or missed jury…
item.content:encoded:
Florida law enforcement is warning about new twists on cryptocurrency scams.


FDLE says criminals are increasingly pitching fake investments claiming cryptocurrency will be used to buy equipment or infrastructure for artificial intelligence processing.


Other scammers are demanding cryptocurrency payments for supposed arrest warrants or missed jury duty.


FDLE reminds Floridians that law enforcement agencies do not accept cryptocurrency to clear warrants or resolve missed jury duty.
